needsBespoke.why: Sovereign's Domination (Possession) replaces Viego's entire kit with a slain enemy champion's abilities, items and base stats for 10 seconds. The closed primitive list has no entry for 'temporarily become an arbitrary other champion with their own kit and item effects' (form-or-stance only covers a champion's own predefined alternate forms with known abilities, not an open-ended possessed kit). This cannot be simulated generically against a dummy without picking a specific champion to possess, which is out of scope for a single champion's kit fight; it also cannot occur in the specified fights at all since it requires a champion takedown, which never happens against a stationary dummy or in a single enemy rotation. We treat Possession as unreachable/inapplicable in both fight types and exclude it from the rotation and primitives beyond noting its dependency structure.

options: Both effects apply simultaneously on the same attack as separate instances, each rolling crit independently
The second strike replaces or otherwise interacts with the passive on-hit so they are not simply additive

unsettled.question: In Q's active-damage crit formula (ViegoQ#TotalDamage / ViegoR#TotalDamage), does 'critChance' mean the champion's actual crit chance stat is multiplied in (partial credit even without guaranteed crit), or does this only apply when an actual crit roll occurs (i.e., the ability either fully crits or doesn't, and the formula is just how big that crit is)?
options: Damage scales continuously with crit chance stat every cast (expected-value smoothing, no randomness)
The ability rolls to crit like a normal attack and only applies the bonus multiplier on a successful crit roll

unsettled.question: Does W's charge time matter in an optimal damage rotation, i.e. should Viego always charge W to max (3s) for max stun/range, or fire it immediately at minimum charge, given that damage magnitude (Damage=[80/135/190/245/300]+100%AP) is fixed regardless of charge time and only stun/range scale with charge?
options: W damage is fixed regardless of charge duration, so casting it with minimal charge is always damage-optimal in a dummy fight since CC does not matter here
Charging W longer meaningfully delays the attack-reset/damage window and interacts with rotation timing, making minimum charge not obviously optimal
quotes: '''Viego''' {{tip|channel|charges}} up to a short time to increase the {{sti|range}} and stun of his blast.

proposal: Start the fight with a basic attack to begin building auto-attack damage and Blade of the Ruined King on-hit rider.

Cast Q (Blade of the Ruined King active) to apply its line damage and mark the target, then continue basic attacking to consume the mark for the second strike and passive on-hit percent-health damage.

Weave R (Heartbreaker) on cooldown against the dummy: it deals AD-ratio physical damage plus a large missing-health-based bonus to the primary (only) target, and triggers an automatic follow-up basic attack.

Use W (Spectral Maw) on cooldown: charge briefly (since damage is fixed regardless of charge time) then recast immediately to fire the magic damage blast, which also resets the basic attack timer, then resume auto-attacking.
Maintain uptime in Harrowed Path's (E) mist zone once cast, for the bonus attack speed buff, without unnecessary movement away from it.
Repeat: weave Q (active + auto-attack mark consumption) and R and W on cooldown, prioritizing whichever comes off cooldown first, while auto-attacking between casts to maximize on-hit procs.

Do not cast Harrowed Path or Sovereign's Domination for their non-damage components (movement/camo/heal), since the dummy fight has no takedowns to spawn Mist Wraiths and stealth/movement do not affect damage.
questions: Should E (Harrowed Path) be cast at all in the damage fight, given its only useful effect there (attack speed) requires standing in a mist zone that must be actively positioned, and does the increased attack speed outweigh the lost auto-attack-timer windows from casting it?

Is there a canonical optimal charge time for W in a no-CC-matters dummy fight, or is minimum charge (near-instant recast) always correct since the value list only shows damage as flat+AP with no charge-time term?

Does the simulator model the mark-consumption second strike and passive on-hit as simultaneously applying on every basic attack landed on a freshly-marked target, or does the mark only get set up once per fight and rarely get reapplied given Q's cooldown, meaningfully limiting how many second strikes occur in 15s?

How should the auto-attack windup/interaction with Q's active cast time (which scales with attack speed) be sequenced against R's automatic post-strike attack command, to avoid clipping or wasting attack timer resets?
